findings.reason: the design must either land the convergence by granting the dispatch.py/mcp_views.py scope it needs, or state the migration as its own node; as written §16 reads implementable while its central deliverable is absent and the duplication it exists to remove survives.
findings.text: §16 designs `section_prose` as "the one public reader" of a plan's authored text and states that `authored_plan_text`, `_section_response` and `_plan_section_text` will each read it, but no `section_prose` exists in the package and each of those three consumers still owns its own soup walk (`reckon/mcp_views.py:2061 authored_plan_text` with `scope.stripped_strings` at :2072, `reckon/mcp_views.py:2238 _section_response`, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:308 _plan_section_text`); the same prose slice-and-strip is additionally re-derived twice inside `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` (`_section_digests` at :302 and `_fingerprint_forms` at :504 both call `_prose_slices` + `strip_tags`)

findings.reason: the section must correct which surface it adds and either make the stripper private again (which requires `section_prose` to land) or justify `strip_tags` as public, so a reader checking the count against the code reconciles.
findings.text: §16's interface accounting says "one public definition is added here, `section_prose` … the stripper beneath it is private", but the code has no `section_prose` and instead exports `strip_tags` publicly (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1880`), read across the package boundary from `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:302,504`; the family's +1 (1478→1480 at §17, →1481 here) is therefore attributed to a name that does not exist while the name that does exist is labelled private

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the fingerprint concern hides bucketing, digesting and the coverage join behind `plan_fingerprint` (public) plus two module-private functions `_section_digests` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:296`) and `_review_coverage` (`:510`); the interface is smaller than the behaviour and adds no helper surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the design converges three duplicate prose readers onto one owner but the owner (`reckon/_plan_html.py:section_prose`) does not exist at head; the three BeautifulSoup text walkers the section promised to retire are all still present.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 names `section_prose` (absent at head) as its one public addition and calls the stripper private, while the surface actually added is the public `strip_tags`, so the section does not account for the interface it shipped.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §16 runs the reuse map by census rather than memory (`grep -rn 'stripped_strings' reckon/`, `_TAG_RE`, `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`, the section-spelling regex sweep) and cites the owners it extends, each of which exists at head (`reckon/_plan_html.py:401 plan_headings`, `:415 structured_section_spans`, `:90 section_record_id`, `reckon/roadmap.py:107 implementable_sections`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 explicitly justifies extending the existing mechanism instead of paralleling it: `structured_section_spans` gains the `every_marked_element` keyword rather than a second slicer, and `_strip_tags` is defined over `_plan_html._TAG_RE` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1876`) rather than re-spelling the expression.
